text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression in nightly workload after the kv-cache change. 50% of token-side latency now spikes intermittently. I ran a perfetto/nsys pass, attached timestamps in the trace.

sam: Can you paste the nsys command you used? and which image?

maya: ran inside the same staging container we use for bench: `docker run --rm -it --gpus all -v $(pwd):/app:ro staging:2026-03-16 /bin/bash` then `nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=nvtx,cuda python -m bench.load_test --profile` trace saved to /tmp/run1.qdrep

jun: quick note — the lines are missing only for kernels when kv-cache hits. When we warm the cache the kernel shows up as `matmul_opt.so` (a precompiled fused kernel bundle) which likely was built without debug info. When cache misses we fall back to `libaten.so` kernels that do have lineinfo.

katie: that matches my local repro. warm run -> missing source lines in nsys UI. cold run -> lines present. So it's not CUPTI stripping per se.

perf-bot: aggregate shows hotspots: `matmul_fused` (shadowing from prebuilt bundle) 60% of GPU time, `softmax_kv_cache` 15%, rest spread.

maya: suspected cause: packaging step for the fused kernel bundle strips symbols to reduce image size. Build logs show we run `objcopy --strip-debug` for `matmul_opt.so`.

sam: can we confirm build-id vs container path mismatch? sometimes objcopy keeps build-id but nsys can't find debuginfo if `/usr/lib/debug` isn't mounted. run `eu-readelf -n matmul_opt.so | grep Build ID` inside container and on host to compare.

maya: ran that — build-id present, but nsys symbolizer tries to find `/usr/lib/debug/.build-id/xx/xxxxx.debug` and our builder stores debug files at `/debug_store/builds/` (different root). So pathmap missing.

jun: two quick options: (1) ship debuglink into same container path or (2) configure nsys/addr2line to use `--path` mapping. For nsys/`nsys-ui` you can set `NSYS_SYMBOL_PATH`? (not real env var) — actually the symbolizer respects `LOCAL_PROFILER_SYMBOL_PATH` (from our internal stack). We should document how to point it.

katie: alternative cheap fix: include debug symlink tree under `/usr/lib/debug/.build-id` in the staging image pointing to our debug store. small and non-sensitive.

sam: also worth checking CUPTI vs driver mismatch. If CUPTI can't hook, nsys leaves entries as raw addresses. Which `libcupti.so` version is in the image? `ldd $(which nsys)`?

maya: built image has `libcupti.so.11.8` while driver on host is 12.x in CI machines. But for the runs the container uses host driver libs via the NVIDIA mount, so CUPTI 11.8 inside container + driver 12 -> some trace metadata gaps observed. However those gaps affect only NVTX metadata; CUDA kernel symbolization still comes from ELF mapping.

perf-bot: correlation check: host driver mismatch increases missing NVTX ranges by 8% in our sample set, not the dominant factor here.

jun: root cause summary so far: kernel selection heuristic prefers a prebuilt fused kernel when kv-cache is hot. That fused bundle lacks debuginfo in the image due to objcopy strip. Because of build-path mapping differences, even our external debug bundles aren't being found by the symbolizer. So traces show anonymous addresses for the dominant hotspot.

maya: proposed fixes: 1) change kernel packaging to keep split debug artifacts (objcopy --only-keep-debug) and include debug tree in staging images behind a feature flag; 2) update our trace collection docs with explicit debug mount instructions and a helper script to populate `/usr/lib/debug/.build-id` from our debug store; 3) add a CI check that runs nsys on a minimal warm/cold scenario and fails if dominant kernel lacks symbolization (heuristic: top kernel >30% time and <1% lines mapped).

katie: I can add the helper script, something like: 
```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
DEBUG_STORE=/debug_store/builds
DST=/usr/lib/debug/.build-id
mkdir -p "$DST"
find "$DEBUG_STORE" -type f -name '*.debug' -exec bash -c 'id=$(basename {} | cut -c1-2); mkdir -p "$DST/$id"; cp {} "$DST/$id/$(basename {} | sed s/\.debug//)"' \;
```

sam: for short-term debugging we can also run nsys with `--external-symbols=/debug_store/builds` and pass `--symbol-search-paths` (see docs) to avoid rebuilding images.

jun: long-term we should consider embedding lightweight symbol metadata in the kernel bundle (a minimal symbol map that maps function names to offsets) so trace UIs can at least show function names even without full source lines. Might be valuable for fused kernels shipped to customers.

infra-bot: deploy notice: rolled back the KV cache warm-run change in staging at commit `c2a9f3d` at 2026-03-17T21:05:12Z. If you need the specific image tag, ask ops.

maya: thanks. I'll open a short RFC for: keep-split-debug + trace helper + CI symbolization smoke test. Will paste links to the repro trace and perfetto timeline in the PR.

sam: 👍 please include exact nsys commands and the eu-readelf build-id output in the PR so SRE can debug image packaging.

maya: will do. attaching quick repro commands in the PR and the qdrep in ARTIFACTS.

katie: I also added a checklist to the PR for devs: build with `-g`, run `objcopy --only-keep-debug`, keep artifact in debug-store, ensure image contains `/usr/lib/debug/.build-id` mapping.

jun: one more note — when we test locally, use `nsys profile --stats=true --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi` and `perfetto` export. perfetto HTML shows the kernel timeline and you can cross-check addresses with `addr2line -e matmul_opt.so 0xADDR`.

maya: perfect. I'll queue the PR and ping infra/sre for the env mapping change.

sam: thanks team. If anyone hits the trace-symbolization blocker in other threads, link this one.

perf-bot: follow-up: scheduled nightly symbolization scan tomorrow 06:00 UTC to detect other prebuilt bundles missing debuginfo.
